title: Pip and the Helper School

sentences.text: Pip and the Helper School.

pages.scene_description: Pip the robot owl on a moonlit windowsill, a glowing school sign behind.

sentences.text: Pip is a small robot owl.
She reads the news each night.
Tonight, one story makes her feathers fluff up.

pages.scene_description: Pip in a cozy nest of books, reading a tiny glowing newspaper.

sentences.text: Carnegie Mellon and Microsoft started a program called PRAISE.
It helps new software engineers use AI tools well.
Software engineers write the code that makes apps work.

pages.scene_description: Pip's newspaper shows a university and a tech company shaking hands.

sentences.text: The new engineers take classes online.
They also get a coach who knows the job well.

pages.scene_description: Pip flies over an office where a senior engineer helps a new one.

sentences.text: Jace Watson's college did not teach him much about AI tools.
A leader saw that AI helps skilled engineers more than new ones.
Maybe new tools feel hard when no one shows you how.

pages.scene_description: Pip holds a strange new tool and looks puzzled.

sentences.text: Mark Russinovich is a leader at Microsoft.
He said AI does not remove the need for new engineers.
Pip likes that.
Everyone has to start somewhere.

pages.scene_description: A kind grown-up at a whiteboard, with Pip listening.

sentences.text: Now the engineers learn in class and with a coach.
Their classes can count toward a master's degree.

pages.scene_description: Pip claps her wings in a classroom full of smiles.

sentences.text: Pip thinks smart tools work best with people who keep learning.
Maybe one day you will learn with an AI tool and a good teacher.

pages.scene_description: Pip settles into her nest under the stars.

sentences.text: Carnegie Mellon and Microsoft launched PRAISE.
sentences.source_quote: Carnegie Mellon and Microsoft launched the Preceptorship

sentences.text: New engineers get coaching from senior engineers at Microsoft.
sentences.source_quote: plus hands-on mentorship from senior engineers at Microsoft

sentences.text: The idea started with a visit to CMU in October 2025.
sentences.source_quote: The idea came from an October 2025 visit to CMU

pages.scene_description: A simple page with real facts and source tags.

sentences.text: Quiz time! Let's see what you remember.

pages.scene_description: Pip holds up three glowing cards.

parent_card.concept: AI tools help people work, but people still need to learn and grow.
parent_card.background: Carnegie Mellon and Microsoft started PRAISE, a program where new software engineers take classes and get coached by senior engineers on using AI tools well.
parent_card.question: Who is someone who helps you learn new things?
parent_card.honest_answer: Even with smart AI tools, people learn best with teachers and helpers. A Microsoft leader said AI does not remove the need for new engineers.

key_facts: Carnegie Mellon and Microsoft started a program called PRAISE.
New engineers in PRAISE get coaching from senior engineers.
A Microsoft leader said AI does not remove the need for new engineers.
